walkthrough: Identify the situation: source frequency $f_s = 846\text{ Hz}$, source speed $v_s = 25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, wave speed $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, observer stationary.
State the Doppler rule: maximum heard frequency occurs when the source velocity is directly toward the observer, compressing successive wavefronts.
Use the approaching-source equation $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$ because the effective wavelength is $(v - v_s)/f_s$.
Substitute values with units: $f_o = 846\text{ Hz} \times 340\text{ m s}^{-1}/(340\text{ m s}^{-1} - 25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 846 \times 340/315\text{ Hz}$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $340/315 \approx 1.0794$, so $f_o \approx 846 \times 1.0794 \approx 913\text{ Hz}$, with unit $\text{Hz}$ as required.
Connect to the options: the value about $913\text{ Hz}$ is greater than the source frequency as expected for approach, while $788\text{ Hz}$ is the receding minimum. This is option D.
